sheet-81.description: The southern end of Edgewater (then the borough of Undercliff), Bergen County, where it meets North Bergen in Hudson County below the Palisades, drawn at 80 ft to an inch. A single road, lettered Hoboken & Hudson River Turnpike (today's River Road, whose old line the county boundary still follows east of the present roadway), crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right; the boundary between Bergen and Hudson counties runs along its river-side edge and turns towards the river at the left edge and up the cliff at the right edge. North-west of the road the sheet is blank and lettered Hudson Co., with key numbers 128 and 129 pointing to the Hudson County sheets. Church St. leaves the turnpike towards the cliff. Along the river side of the turnpike stands a row of about twenty small frame dwellings and shops, numbered 1188 to 1212, with a few more scattered buildings and a vacant dwelling at no. 1234. Below them long lot lines run down to the shore, where the works of the Bulls Ferry Chemical Co. are shown only in outline, marked Survey Refused: a stable, several sheds and long buildings, all without detail. The shore is drawn with an inlet or slip reaching inland, and the open Hudson River fills the lower half of the sheet, crossed by the dashed exterior line for solid filling. A compass rose, a scale bar (1 inch = 80 feet) and the neighbouring sheet numbers 80 and 82 are printed in the margins.
notes: Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike is today's River Road; near the left edge of the sheet the modern road runs some 50 m west of the old line, which the county boundary still follows.
Church St. corresponds to the south end of today's Churchill Road.
Bulls Ferry Chemical Co. works drawn in outline only (Survey Refused).
Exterior line for solid filling (harbour line) drawn in the river.

Map, 80 ft to an inch (scale bar). Edgewater (then Undercliff) at the Hudson County line, south of Shadyside: Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike (now River Road, the old line partly followed by the county boundary east of today's River Road), Church St. (now Churchill Road), a row of dwellings nos. 1188-1264, Bulls Ferry Chemical Co. (survey refused), shore and exterior line for solid filling. North-west of the turnpike is Hudson County (blank, key nos. 128, 129). No surviving street junction except Church St.; placed by hand-picked control on the drawn county boundary corners and Church St. One part. North arrow about 9 degrees anticlockwise of true north (magnetic).

sheet-82.description: Shadyside, at the south end of Edgewater (then Undercliff) in Bergen County, between the foot of the Palisades and the Hudson River, drawn at 80 ft to an inch. River Road (today's Old River Road) crosses the top of the sheet, with Gorge Road branching off it towards the north-east. Above the road, on the slope, a small subdivision is laid out in narrow lots along Gomez Road, Terrace Ave. and Cascade Ave., with a regulating tank at the top left; the boundary between Hudson and Bergen counties leaves River Road there and climbs the cliff. Along River Road and Gorge Road stand frame dwellings, stores and a hay and feed store. Below the road, River Street and Meadow Ave. border a few blocks with the Davis & Arundell iron foundry, and the Road to Shadyside Landing runs down to the river past a row of small houses. Most of the sheet is taken up by two large chemical works on the shore: the General Chemical Co., with sulphuric acid chambers, pyrites burners, towers, muriatic and nitric acid stills, a platina still room, a paper house, salt cake and soda plants, a boiler house, carpenter, pipe and repair shops and a long dock shed on a pier; and to the west the Barrett Mfg. Co. tar works with tar and oil tanks, still houses, storage sheds and an ammonia house. A reference table lists the plant letters, and notes the works' own fire department. At the left edge the Standard Oil Co. premises are marked vacant, beside a slip. The Hudson River and the exterior line for solid filling fill the bottom of the sheet.
notes: River Road on the sheet is today's Old River Road; the present River Road runs east of it over the former works.

Gomez Road, Terrace Ave., Cascade Ave., River Street, Meadow Ave. and the Road to Shadyside Landing are not in the modern street data; modern Gorge Road crosses Old River Road about 50 m west of where the landing road met it.
General Chemical Co. works (sulphuric, muriatic, nitric and acetic acid plants) and Barrett Mfg. Co. tar works; Standard Oil Co. premises vacant.
The north arrow points about 10 degrees anticlockwise of true north as fitted (magnetic north).

Map, 80 ft to an inch (scale bar). Shadyside, Edgewater: River Road (now Old River Road), Gorge Road, Gomez Road, Terrace and Cascade Avenues (on the Palisades slope), River Street and Meadow Ave. (gone), Road to Shadyside Landing (gone), General Chemical Co. sulphuric acid works, Barrett Mfg. Co. tar works, Standard Oil Co. (vacant), Davis & Arundell iron foundry. No modern junction survives; placed by hand-picked control: the county-line corner, the bend of Old River Road and a shape fit of the drawn River Road, Gorge Road and county line to the modern lines. One part. North arrow about 9 degrees anticlockwise of true north (magnetic).
